title: sse: fix partial-JSON delimiter/token/event ordering causing broken structured streaming
author: Elena Morris
description:
Motivation: We observed multiple customer reports and flaky internal e2e failures where SSE streamed responses containing structured JSON payloads (OpenAI compatibility 'data:' chunks and partial JSON bodies) were being reassembled incorrectly by the streaming parser. Root causes included: 1) delimiter tokens ("data:" boundaries and SSE event separators) being handled out-of-order when a JSON token crossed an SSE chunk boundary, 2) naive UTF-8 rune splitting creating invalid byte sequences during concatenation, and 3) race conditions between the assembler and the parser state machine when concurrent streams were multiplexed.

Summary: This PR fixes SSE chunking/framing bugs in the streaming parser and OpenAI compatibility layer to ensure correct ordering and atomic reassembly of partial JSON payloads. The change introduces a buffer-aware assembler that preserves token boundaries, normalizes delimiter handling for both 'data: ' lines and '[DONE]' markers, ensures correct UTF-8 rune handling across chunk boundaries, and serializes assembler operations per-stream to remove races. The change is backward compatible at the API level (no contract changes) and includes additional unit/integration tests plus diagnostic metrics to detect future regressions.

What I changed: see commit list below for a short summary. High-level: - Replace ad-hoc chunk glue logic with a deterministic assembler that tracks parsing state (inside-string, escape sequences, bracket depth) so partial JSON objects are only emitted when syntactically complete. - Normalize SSE delimiter handling: accept both 'data: ' prefixed chunks and bare JSON fragments; treat '

' (SSE event end) as an emitter boundary but do not assume it aligns with JSON token boundaries. - Add robust UTF-8 joiner to avoid splitting multi-byte runes across buffers. - Make assembler per-stream and single-threaded via an internal stream lock to avoid interleaving when events are parsed concurrently. - Add a set of reproducible fuzz/integration tests that exercise partial JSON split at arbitrary byte offsets, and a regression test reproducing the customer report.

Compatibility notes: This fixes behavioral correctness for streaming structured outputs. No API user-visible changes; the SDKs and compatibility wrappers now see the same event ordering and complete JSON objects as before the regression. Consumers relying on invalid partial emission ordering will no longer see that behavior (this is intended).

Testing: Unit tests added for assembler state machine (string escapes, nested objects, array streaming), integration tests for OpenAI-compatible SSE stream reassembly, and a new e2e test that streams a large multi-field structured response split at many offsets. CI: we re-ran the e2e suite after the fix; an initial flaky integration test failed on first run (intermittent due to test environment timing) but passed on rerun.

Rollout & Monitoring: Added a diagnostic metric 'streaming.partial_json_reassembly_errors' (increments on any parse failure) and a 7-day alert baseline. We will monitor for customer reports and rollback if unexpected regressions appear.

Notes for reviewers: see inline comments in the diff for details on the assembler state transition table and the UTF-8 joiner implementation. The change touches runtime streaming code and the OpenAI compatibility shim; please pay attention to concurrency boundaries and GC behavior for large streaming responses.

Related: Linear ENG-4578 (streaming stability), ENG-4621 (openai compat regression).

Elena Morris (author): Addressed the stream-id issue and serialized assembler ops using an internal mutex per stream. Added a unit test that spawns concurrent deliveries to the same stream to validate ordering.
Aisha Patel (reviewer): Request to add tests for unicode rune boundaries; asked to verify performance impact of utf8 joiner on large streams.
Elena Morris (author): Added utf8 tests and microbenchmarks; observed negligible overhead (~0.5% for pathological streams). Documented in the changelog comment in parser.go.

merge_commit_message:
sse: fix partial-JSON delimiter/token/event ordering causing broken structured streaming

Deterministic assembler, UTF-8 joiner, per-stream serialization, tests
release_notes: Fixes streaming parser reassembly for SSE/OpenAI-compatible streams where JSON tokens crossed event chunk boundaries. Fix prevents malformed partial JSON emissions and restores correct structured output ordering. No API changes.
